environment.test_data: isolated temporary directories; no live application data

directly_observed_run.source_state: After atomic poll-directory preparation, recovery metadata synchronization, and prepared-orphan regression; before the root agent's final release of the closed writer reference.

subsequent_validation_reported_by_root.description: After clearing the closed writer reference in filestore finalization.

full_http_recovery.scope: Real application SIGKILL and restart within and after the original voting window.

subsequent_validation_reported_by_root.provenance: Reported by the root agent; this report did not rerun those commands.

checks: A blocked sync cannot emit a successful receipt.
Several independent frames share one durable group sync.
Short writes are completed before sync.
Write ENOSPC and sync EIO produce unknown outcomes and poison the writer.
Cancellation after enqueue may leave a persisted unknown attempt.
Logical queue plus one active batch remains bounded.
Admission at 59.9 seconds may finish syncing after 60 seconds.
A deadline observed with a full queue remains closed after clock rollback.
Invalid, not-open, busy, and closed attempts receive the expected status.
Independent header and payload CRC checks reject corruption at EOF and in the middle.
Malformed count, length, sequence, kind, token, choice, admission timestamp, or reserved bytes are rejected.
The complete frame is validated before visiting its votes.
Frames and stray bytes after CLOSED are rejected.
Incomplete header and payload tails are distinguished from complete-frame CRC corruption.
The parent observes an actual successful receipt, SIGKILLs the writer, and verifies it with a separate reader process.
During a later append, the writer emits READY only after a real partial file write; the parent then sends SIGKILL.
Independent readers preserve the acknowledged prefix and report incomplete tails for both partial-header and partial-payload crashes.
An active journal resumes with the original deadline and next frame sequence.
An expired journal seals without extending admission.
Recovered CLOSED state cannot reopen.
Only incomplete final frames are truncated; CRC corruption remains unchanged.
Concurrent writers and recovery owners are excluded by OS locks.
Existing unrelated or symlinked data is rejected without replacement.
Create, Get, List, Vote, Results, FinalizeDue, Ping, and Close are exercised.
The HTTP 32-character lowercase hexadecimal token receives a durable recorded receipt with HTTP 202; UUID-form tokens and invalid tokens are rejected.
Concurrent repeated attempts preserve the first full-token choice during final counting.
Multiple-choice option counts and unique-voter totals agree.
Active and finalized application repository restarts preserve definitions, results, and admission boundaries.
Pending results contain every option and never expose a partial final count.
Overlapping concurrent poll creation is serialized while adjacent windows are accepted.
Published definitions are defensively copied.
Definition-only and fully initialized unpublished preparation directories do not block recovery of an existing acknowledged poll.
Preparation orphans remain inspectable and do not become public polls.
Exceeding the exact unique-voter limit leaves results pending and latches an unhealthy finalization state.
A higher computation budget after restart completes counting from the preserved journal.
A finalized result remains unchanged across repeated finalization and restart.

read_only_review.scope: Current filestore lifecycle, atomic creation/result publication, recovery parser sharing, ownership, limits, and finalizer release of the closed writer.

limitations: These are bounded correctness tests, not a throughput or 100-million-voter capacity measurement.
SIGKILL leaves the kernel and storage device alive; it does not emulate a power cut, host loss, device failure, or a filesystem that violates sync guarantees.
The repository has one durable disk copy and no automatic replica failover.
CRC detects corruption but cannot reconstruct damaged acknowledged data.
Recovered complete unknown attempts can contribute to the final count; a receipt confirms an attempt, not online canonical deduplication.
The original stored voting window is preserved; restart latency at the full workload size has not been established by these tests.
Startup validates historical journals, and exact final counting consumes memory proportional to unique full tokens up to the configured bound.
Partial-root initialization and corruption fail closed and may require operator inspection; known unpublished poll/result preparation files are preserved.
The application currently stores one 40-byte frame header plus one 28-byte vote payload per HTTP attempt; packed-frame benchmark rates do not establish HTTP capacity.
Linux fsync support exists but was not exercised by this Darwin runtime test series.
